text: In 1995, an archaeological excavation was carried out at the farm of Mosfell in the location where the modern road runs up to the church to the north of the graveyard. On this location, archaeologists uncovered stone walls which probably made up part of a medieval church. In the last few summers, however, excavations have focused on the archaeological remains at Hrísbrú. Egils Saga and the Saga of Gunnlaug Worms-Tongue mention a church at Hrísbrú. Oral tradition from the valley has maintained the name Kirkjuhóll (Church Knoll) for one of the small hills at Hrísbrú. The mention in the sagas and the evidence from the local oral tradition suggested a fruitful location for archaeological research.
